name: self_check_eba
prose: Precondition: ubi is a valid UBI device with its volumes array and vtbl_slots, and ai_fastmap and ai_scan are valid attach information objects built by fastmap and by scanning. Postcondition: this is self_check_eba. It allocates two arrays of per-volume pointers (-ENOMEM if either allocation fails) and, for every existing volume, two arrays with one entry per reserved PEB, filled with UBI_LEB_UNMAPPED and then with the PEB numbers of the LEBs found in the scan and fastmap attach info (-ENOMEM if an allocation fails, after freeing what was allocated). For each LEB that is mapped in both it compares the two PEB numbers and, on a mismatch, logs the LEB and both PEB numbers and calls ubi_assert(0); a LEB mapped in only one of them is not reported, and the comparison is skipped for a volume that is missing from either attach info. The mismatch report is not an error return: the function returns 0 whether or not a mismatch was found (what ubi_assert(0) does depends on the kernel configuration), and -ENOMEM only on allocation failure. All allocated arrays are freed before returning.
note: Not a drop: the slice 1549-1714 starts inside self_check_eba (ubi/eba.c:1527-1615), a real function whose head was cut. The old prose said it returned a negative errno if the tables disagree; the code only logs and calls ubi_assert(0) for a mismatch and returns 0, returning -ENOMEM only for allocation failures. I read the whole function.

name: ubi_io_read_vid_hdr
prose: Precondition: pnum is a valid physical eraseblock number (0 <= pnum < ubi->peb_count, checked only by ubi_assert) and vidb has a buffer of at least ubi->vid_hdr_shift + UBI_VID_HDR_SIZE bytes. Postcondition: it reads vid_hdr_shift + UBI_VID_HDR_SIZE bytes at offset ubi->vid_hdr_aloffset of PEB pnum into the buffer with ubi_io_read and returns the read error at once if it is anything other than 0, UBI_IO_BITFLIPS or an ECC error (-EBADMSG); the header is then interpreted from the buffer. If the magic is wrong: with an ECC error from the read it returns UBI_IO_BAD_HDR_EBADMSG; otherwise if the header area is all 0xFF it returns UBI_IO_FF, or UBI_IO_FF_BITFLIPS if the read had reported bitflips; otherwise it returns UBI_IO_BAD_HDR. If the magic is right but the CRC is wrong it returns UBI_IO_BAD_HDR when the read reported no error, and UBI_IO_BAD_HDR_EBADMSG when the read reported either an ECC error or bitflips. If the CRC is right but validate_vid_hdr rejects the header it logs and returns -EINVAL. For a valid header with a read that reported bitflips or an ECC error it returns UBI_IO_BITFLIPS. For a valid header read without error it returns 0, unless the debug fault-injection hooks are enabled, in which case it may return -EIO (emulated read failure), UBI_IO_FF, UBI_IO_FF_BITFLIPS, UBI_IO_BAD_HDR or UBI_IO_BAD_HDR_EBADMSG instead. The header is left in vidb's buffer in all these cases except the early read-error return.
note: Reviewer right: a bad CRC with UBI_IO_BITFLIPS also returns UBI_IO_BAD_HDR_EBADMSG (ubi/io.c:1069-1072: 'if (!read_err) BAD_HDR else BAD_HDR_EBADMSG'), not only for an ECC error; the old prose said the EBADMSG variant meant the MTD layer reported an ECC error. Also made precise: the bad-magic case returns EBADMSG only for a real ECC error, and a valid header with an ECC error read returns UBI_IO_BITFLIPS (1081-1082). Slice cut the head; function at 1015-1111 (name was right).

name: ubi_create_volume
prose: Precondition: the caller holds ubi->device_mutex; req has been validated by the caller: req->alignment is non-zero and at most the LEB size, req->vol_type is dynamic or static, req->name_len matches req->name, and req->vol_id is UBI_VOL_NUM_AUTO or below ubi->vtbl_slots (this function checks none of these; an alignment of 0 would divide by zero). Postcondition: this is ubi_create_volume. It returns -EROFS if ubi->ro_mode is set and -ENOMEM if the volume object cannot be allocated. Under ubi->volumes_lock it picks a free volume id if UBI_VOL_NUM_AUTO was requested (-ENFILE if none; req->vol_id is updated with the chosen id), returns -EEXIST if that id is in use or a live volume with the same name exists, computes usable_leb_size and reserved_pebs, and returns -ENOSPC if more PEBs are reserved than ubi->avail_pebs, otherwise moves them from avail_pebs to rsvd_pebs. It fills in the volume, flushes pending erases for that volume id with ubi_wl_flush and creates the EBA table with ubi_eba_create_table (their errors are returned after the PEB reservation is undone), sets the used-eraseblock counters, then publishes the volume in ubi->volumes and increments vol_count, registers the character device with cdev_device_add, writes the volume table record with ubi_change_vtbl_record and, on success, sends UBI_VOLUME_ADDED, runs self_check_volumes and returns 0. If cdev_device_add fails (error returned) the slot and vol_count are restored and the reservation undone; if ubi_change_vtbl_record fails the device is removed with cdev_device_del first, then the same rollback. On every failure it drops the device reference with put_device (the volume object is freed by vol_release) and logs 'cannot create volume'. It has no -EINVAL return (vmt.c:165-349).
note: Reviewer wrong: the function does not return -EINVAL; the checks for vol_type, alignment and vol_id are not in ubi_create_volume (vmt.c:165-349), so they belong to the caller, and the code would misbehave (division by zero, out-of-range volumes[] index) without them. The old failure list was right. Slice cut the head; the name was right.

name: wear_leveling_worker
prose: Precondition: this is the UBI work-queue callback wear_leveling_worker(ubi, wrk, shutdown); wrk is a kmalloc'ed work item owned by the callee, and the caller holds none of ubi->fm_eba_sem, ubi->move_mutex or ubi->wl_lock (the function takes them itself). Postcondition: it frees wrk first; if shutdown is non-zero it returns 0 doing nothing else; it returns -ENOMEM if the VID buffer cannot be allocated. Otherwise it takes fm_eba_sem for read, move_mutex and wl_lock and picks the source e1 (removed from the used tree, from the scrub tree when scrubbing, or the fastmap anchor case) and the target e2 from get_peb_for_wl; if no free PEB or no used/scrub PEB exists, or the erase-count difference is below UBI_WL_THRESHOLD (e2 is then given back to the free tree), it clears ubi->wl_scheduled and returns 0 (out_cancel). Otherwise it records move_from/move_to, drops wl_lock, reads the VID header of e1 and calls ubi_eba_copy_leb. If the move succeeds it puts e2 in the used tree (unless move_to_put is set) and erases e1 synchronously (and e2 if it was put meanwhile) and returns 0. If the move is abandoned without an error (no VID header or bit-flips in an empty header, ECC error on a fast-attached device, MOVE_CANCEL_RACE, MOVE_RETRY, target-side bit-flips or errors, or a source read error while erroneous_peb_count is within max_erroneous) e1 goes back to the protection queue, the erroneous tree, the scrub tree or the used tree, or is erased in the fast-attach ECC case, e2 is returned to the free tree (when it is known clean) or erased synchronously (with torture for target errors), and the function returns 0. If any of the synchronous erases fail, ubi_ro_mode is called and the error is returned. Any other failure (other read errors on the VID header, a negative error from ubi_eba_copy_leb, too many erroneous PEBs) logs, clears move_from/move_to, destroys both e1 and e2 with wl_entry_destroy and calls ubi_ro_mode. On the error exits it returns err if negative and -EIO otherwise (a positive status such as MOVE_SOURCE_RD_ERR becomes -EIO). Every return after the locks are taken has released wl_lock, move_mutex and fm_eba_sem, and the VID buffer is freed on all of them. An unrecognised positive status from ubi_eba_copy_leb hits ubi_assert(0) and then falls through to the success path.
note: Reviewer 2 right in substance, but the old prose had the bigger error: it said the locks and e1/e2 were already held/chosen by the caller (head above the slice), but the real function (wl.c:661-1020) takes fm_eba_sem, move_mutex and wl_lock itself (681-683) and removes e1 from used (758) or scrub (770) itself, so I rewrote the precondition. Slice began at 769, i.e. the head was cut. Did not read do_sync_erase, wl_entry_destroy or ubi_eba_copy_leb bodies, so the effect of a failing do_sync_erase on its entry is not claimed.

name: arcnet_interrupt
prose: Precondition: dev_id is the net_device registered as this IRQ's handler data, so netdev_priv(dev) is non-NULL (BUG_ON otherwise), and the call is in hard-IRQ context with the hardware accessors in lp->hw usable. Postcondition: it takes lp->lock with spin_lock_irqsave and every path releases it with the saved flags. retval starts as IRQ_NONE and is the only value returned. (1) If lp->reset_in_progress is set it returns IRQ_NONE immediately. (2) If the interface is not running it clears a pending RESETflag (CFLAGScmd|RESETclear), sets the hardware interrupt mask to 0 and returns IRQ_NONE. (3) Otherwise it loops at most 5 times while the last pass did something: each pass reads the status; if RESETflag is set it logs a spurious reset, sets reset_in_progress, stops the queue, turns the carrier off, schedules lp->reset_work and leaves the loop for the unlock, skipping the interrupt-mask rewrite, and returns whatever retval already holds, which is IRQ_HANDLED if an earlier pass in this call handled something and IRQ_NONE if this was the first pass. Otherwise a pass handles, in order, the receive-complete flag (takes a new receive buffer and starts receive), EXCNAK (disables transmit, sets excnak_pending, drops EXCNAK from the mask), transmit-free or a timed-out transmit (updates the mask, reports ack status through ack_tx or reply_work, releases the transmit buffer, calls go_tx and continue_tx, may free the skb, wakes the queue if no transmit is current), then delivers the received packet with arcnet_rx and releases its buffer, and handles RECON (link-down, timer and recon counters) or the cabling-restored case; didsomething is incremented for receive, EXCNAK, transmit and the received-packet delivery (not for RECON), and a pass with didsomething set ORs IRQ_HANDLED into retval. (4) After the loop ends normally (including when it handled nothing) it sets the hardware interrupt mask to 0, waits 1 microsecond, restores it to lp->intmask, unlocks and returns retval, so the return is IRQ_HANDLED if any pass handled an event and IRQ_NONE otherwise.
note: Reviewers on the RESET path: round-15 reviewer right (arcnet.c:1098 sets IRQ_HANDLED in earlier passes and the RESETflag exit at 903-913 returns retval unchanged, so the result can be IRQ_HANDLED); the earlier 'always IRQ_NONE' reviewer is wrong on that point. Reviewer 'reset and !netif_running paths handle events but return IRQ_NONE' is right for !netif_running (877-882) and for the first-pass reset. Old prose already said 'IRQ_NONE ... if a RESETflag is seen', which was too absolute; fixed. Also RECON does not count as didsomething (1031-1085). Slice 764-1025 cut the head; the function is 854-1112 and the tail of the slice ends before the function's end; I read the whole function. I did not read arcnet_rx, go_tx or the lp->hw ops.

name: rx
prose: Precondition: this is the RFC1201 receive handler rx(dev, bufnum, pkthdr, length). pkthdr points to a readable and writable struct archdr holding the ARCnet hard header and the RFC1201 soft header already copied from card buffer bufnum (the exception-packet path overwrites pkthdr->soft.rfc1201), length is the packet size in the card buffer and is large enough for the header fields used below (not checked here except for exception packets), and the caller serialises calls (it uses per-source state in lp->rfc1201.incoming[pkthdr->hard.source]; the source is a one-byte value so the index is in range). Postcondition: returns void. An exception packet (split_flag 0xFF) shorter than 4+RFC1201_HDR_SIZE is dropped with no change; a longer one has 4 bytes skipped and its soft header re-read from the card. An unsplit packet: any assembly in progress for that source is freed (aborted_seq set to the new sequence, rx_errors and rx_missed_errors counted, in->skb cleared), in->sequence is set to the packet's sequence, then alloc_skb is tried; on failure rx_dropped is counted and it returns with that already-updated state; otherwise the whole packet is copied into a new skb, an ARP packet with a zero source address gets the hardware source and counts rx_crc_errors while a malformed ARP header counts rx_errors and rx_crc_errors, and type_trans sets skb->protocol (it pulls the ARCnet and RFC1201 headers, so netif_rx receives the payload only; an unknown protocol gives protocol 0 and counts rx_errors and rx_crc_errors) and the skb is passed to netif_rx, which takes ownership. A split packet: if an assembly exists with a different sequence it is freed and cleared with rx_errors and rx_missed_errors counted. For a first fragment (split_flag odd) an existing assembly skb is freed (counted as rx_errors and rx_missed_errors) without clearing in->skb, then sequence, numpackets and lastpacket are set; if numpackets > 16 it records aborted_seq, counts rx_errors and rx_length_errors and returns (in->skb is left pointing at the freed skb if one was freed); if alloc_skb fails in->skb becomes NULL, aborted_seq is recorded, rx_dropped counted and it returns; otherwise the headers are copied into the new assembly skb with the split flag cleared. For a later fragment: with no assembly it returns, counting rx_errors and rx_missed_errors unless aborted_seq equals the sequence; a duplicate or old fragment (after in->lastpacket has been incremented) counts rx_errors and rx_frame_errors and returns; an out-of-order fragment frees the assembly, clears in->skb, records aborted_seq, counts rx_errors and rx_missed_errors, resets lastpacket and numpackets and returns. Otherwise the fragment payload is appended to the assembly skb and when lastpacket equals numpackets the assembly state is cleared, type_trans sets the protocol and the skb is passed to netif_rx (which takes ownership).
note: Reviewers right: (1) alloc failure leaves in->sequence updated (rfc1201.c:180-186); (2) netif_rx receives headerless data because type_trans calls skb_pull (92-103); (3) the exception path writes pkthdr->soft (163-164), so the precondition must say writable. Own correction to the old prose: on alloc_skb failure for a first fragment in->skb is set to NULL by the assignment at 292-294, it is not left dangling; only the numpackets > 16 return (284-290) can leave in->skb dangling after a free. Slice 1-255 ended mid-function (rx is 133-375); I read the whole function but not type_trans beyond 92-129, nor the card copy helpers or the length checks in the caller.

name: ad_mux_machine
prose: Precondition: port is a valid struct port whose slave and bond are valid, update_slave_arr points to a writable bool, and the caller holds the RCU read lock and the state-machine context so that rcu_dereference(port->aggregator) is legal; the aggregator pointer is dereferenced without a NULL check in the WAITING, ATTACHED, COLLECTING_DISTRIBUTING and COLLECTING cases and in the post-transition ATTACHED case, so it must be non-NULL there (only the DISTRIBUTING case tests it). Postcondition: returns void, takes no reference and no lock. If AD_PORT_BEGIN is set in port->sm_vars the next state is AD_MUX_DETACHED; otherwise the 802.3ad mux transition is evaluated: DETACHED goes to WAITING when SELECTED or STANDBY; WAITING clears AD_PORT_READY_N, refreshes the aggregator ready flag with __set_agg_ports_ready and goes to DETACHED if the port is no longer selected, else counts down sm_mux_timer_counter (setting AD_PORT_READY_N when it reaches 0), refreshes the aggregator ready flag and goes to ATTACHED when AD_PORT_READY is set and the timer is 0; ATTACHED goes to COLLECTING_DISTRIBUTING (or to COLLECTING when bond->params.coupled_control is false) when selected, the partner is in sync and the aggregation selection timer is not running and the aggregator is active, goes to DETACHED (clearing READY_N and refreshing the ready flag) when no longer selected or on STANDBY, and otherwise sets the actor SYNCHRONIZATION bit if the aggregator is active; COLLECTING_DISTRIBUTING and COLLECTING go back via __port_move_to_attached_state when it applies, else the COLLECTING_DISTRIBUTING case enables the port and sets *update_slave_arr when the aggregator is active and the port is not yet collecting/distributing, while COLLECTING goes to DISTRIBUTING when selected and the partner is in sync and collecting, else when the aggregator is active and the slave rx is disabled calls ad_enable_collecting and sets *update_slave_arr; DISTRIBUTING falls back to COLLECTING when the port is not selected, on STANDBY or when the partner or actor synchronization/collecting bits are missing, else enables the port and sets *update_slave_arr under the same condition. When the state changed it then, for the new state: DETACHED clears the actor SYNCHRONIZATION, COLLECTING and DISTRIBUTING bits, disables collecting/distributing and sets port->ntt; WAITING only reloads sm_mux_timer_counter (AD_WAIT_WHILE_TIMER) and does not touch actor_oper_port_state or ntt; ATTACHED sets or clears actor SYNCHRONIZATION depending on whether the aggregator is active, clears COLLECTING and DISTRIBUTING, disables collecting/distributing and sets ntt; COLLECTING_DISTRIBUTING sets the three actor bits, enables collecting/distributing and sets ntt; COLLECTING sets COLLECTING and SYNCHRONIZATION, clears DISTRIBUTING, enables collecting, disables distributing and sets ntt; DISTRIBUTING sets DISTRIBUTING and SYNCHRONIZATION and enables collecting/distributing without setting ntt.
note: Reviewer right: the WAITING entry (bond_3ad.c:1188-1190) only reloads the timer, it does not update actor_oper_port_state or set ntt, so 'whenever the state changed ... sets ntt' was wrong; ntt is set for DETACHED, ATTACHED, COLLECTING_DISTRIBUTING and COLLECTING (1186,1202,1210,1218) and not for WAITING or DISTRIBUTING (1225). Old prose also omitted the NULL-aggregator hazard (only 1159 checks it). Slice 1040-1299 cut the head (function at 1029-1230). I did not read __port_move_to_attached_state or the ad_enable/disable helpers.

name: bond_enslave
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the rtnl lock, bond_dev is an initialised bonding master, slave_dev is a valid netdevice, and extack may be NULL or used for messages. Postcondition: it returns 0 on success and a negative errno on failure. Checks done first with a plain return and no state change: -EPERM if slave_dev is ARPHRD_CAN, is a master device that is not a bond, is bond_dev itself, is VLAN-challenged while bond_dev uses VLANs, or is already up (IFF_UP); -EBUSY if slave_dev already has an rx handler; -EINVAL if the bond has no slaves, slave_dev is not Ethernet and the mode is 802.3ad, or if the bond has slaves and the device types differ. When the bond has no slaves and the types differ, a failing NETDEV_PRE_TYPE_CHANGE notifier gives -EBUSY, otherwise the bond's uc/mc lists are flushed and the bond device is set up for the slave's type (this is the first state change). Later failures go through the unwind labels: -EOPNOTSUPP for an InfiniBand slave outside active-backup mode, or in active-backup mode for a slave without ndo_set_mac_address (or InfiniBand) when the bond already has slaves and fail_over_mac is not active (with no slaves yet, fail_over_mac is set to active instead); -ENOMEM if bond_alloc_slave fails; errors propagated from bond_set_dev_addr, dev_set_mtu, dev_set_mac_address, dev_open, bond_alb_init_slave (load-balancing modes), vlan_vids_add_by_dev, netdev_rx_handler_register, bond_master_upper_dev_link, bond_sysfs_slave_add, dev_set_promiscuity, dev_set_allmulti and dev_xdp_propagate; -EBUSY if netpoll is enabled on the bond and slave_enable_netpoll fails; and -EOPNOTSUPP if the bond has an XDP program and the slave lacks ndo_bpf/ndo_xdp_xmit or already has an XDP program loaded. On success the slave has the bond's MTU, the bond's MAC address (or a random one for fail_over_mac follow when it would collide, or left alone for fail_over_mac with active-backup), is opened and flagged IFF_BONDING and IFF_NO_ADDRCONF, has its link state set from the miimon/arp_interval parameters, is set up per mode (inactive flags for active-backup and 802.3ad with 3ad bind, active flag for TLB/ALB, active slave and possibly curr_active_slave otherwise), has the rx handler, upper/lower link and sysfs entry installed, has promiscuity, allmulti and multicast sync applied when the bond does not use a primary, the XDP program propagated with an extra reference when the bond has one, bond->slave_cnt incremented and the carrier and slave array updated. On failure the labels err_sysfs_del, err_upper_unlink, err_unregister, err_detach (removes VLAN ids, clears primary_slave and curr_active_slave if they were this slave, reselects, disables netpoll), err_close (clears IFF_BONDING, closes the slave), err_restore_mac, err_restore_mtu, err_free (drops the slave kobject reference) and err_undo_flags (random MAC and ether setup for a slave-less bond whose type had changed) undo the earlier steps in reverse, but the unwind does not reverse every step: after the XDP failures it does not decrement bond->slave_cnt, does not undo bond_slave_ns_maddrs_add, the promiscuity, allmulti or multicast sync, nor the 802.3ad binding or ALB init.
note: Reviewer right: bond_main.c:2282-2286 returns -EOPNOTSUPP (via err_sysfs_del) when the slave already has an XDP program, not in the old list. Old prose overclaimed the unwind: slave_cnt++ (2255) and the promisc/allmulti/mc-sync block (2222-2250) precede the XDP failure gotos at 2272/2286/2293, and the labels at 2315-2375 do not undo them; there is also no bond_3ad_unbind_slave or ALB deinit in the labels. Also corrected the -EOPNOTSUPP condition (only active-backup with slaves, 1969-1981) and -EINVAL conditions (1925-1930, 1955-1958). Slice 2049-2303 cut the head and tail; read whole function 1854-2376 except log and comment lines and the netpoll config details. Large function, read fully but skimmed log lines.

name: bond_check_params
prose: Precondition: called once from module init (__init, bonding_init) with params pointing to writable storage, after the module parameters (mode, xmit_hash_policy, lacp_rate, ad_select, max_bonds, miimon, updelay, downdelay, use_carrier, num_peer_notif, tx_queues, all_slaves_active, resend_igmp, packets_per_slave, arp_interval, arp_ip_target, arp_validate, arp_all_targets, primary, primary_reselect, fail_over_mac, lp_interval, min_links) have been set. Postcondition: it is not pure: it rewrites those module-parameter globals when it normalises them (clamps or resets out-of-range max_bonds, miimon, updelay, downdelay, num_peer_notif, tx_queues, all_slaves_active, resend_igmp, packets_per_slave and lp_interval with warnings; forces miimon to BOND_DEFAULT_MIIMON when the mode does not use ARP monitoring and miimon is 0; when miimon is set it disables arp_interval and divides updelay and downdelay by miimon; disables arp_interval on a bad or missing arp_ip_target; sets primary to NULL when the mode does not use a primary). It returns -EINVAL for an unparsable mode, xmit_hash_policy (only parsed in modes other than round-robin, active-backup and broadcast), lacp_rate (only parsed in 802.3ad mode), ad_select, arp_validate or fail_over_mac string, for use_carrier other than 1, for arp_validate given while arp_interval is 0 (after the normalisation above), for an unparsable primary_reselect when primary is set, and when the default lookups for ad_actor_sys_prio, ad_user_port_key or tlb_dynamic_lb fail; an invalid arp_all_targets only logs an error and uses 0. The -EINVAL returns occur before any of the *params assignments at the end except that params->ad_select is already written (to the parsed value or BOND_AD_STABLE) when later checks (use_carrier, arp_validate, primary_reselect, fail_over_mac, the default lookups) fail, so *params is partially filled on those errors. On success it fills the remaining fields (mode, xmit_policy, miimon, num_peer_notif, arp_interval, arp_validate, arp_all_targets, missed_max=2, updelay, downdelay, peer_notif_delay=0, lacp_active=1, lacp_fast, primary_reselect, fail_over_mac, tx_queues, all_slaves_active, resend_igmp, min_links, lp_interval, packets_per_slave, tlb_dynamic_lb, ad_actor_sys_prio, ad_actor_system zeroed, ad_user_port_key, coupled_control=1, broadcast_neighbor=0, lacp_strict=0, reciprocal_packets_per_slave, primary name if set, arp_targets, ns_targets cleared with IPv6) and returns 0.
note: Reviewer right: bond_main.c:6126/6130 write params->ad_select before the -EINVAL returns at 6160, 6275, 6284, 6340, 6354, 6369, 6377 and 6385, so 'without filling params' was wrong. Also corrected: primary_reselect is only parsed if primary is set (6333); an invalid arp_all_targets is not an error (6295-6298); xmit_hash_policy and lacp_rate are only parsed in the relevant modes (6082-6115). Slice 6118-6372 cut the head; function is 6056-6445; read in full.

name: bond_changelink
prose: Precondition: bond_dev is a bonding net_device (netdev_priv is a struct bonding), data is NULL or an array of parsed IFLA_BOND_* attribute pointers indexed by attribute id, tb is unused here, extack may be used, and the caller holds the rtnl lock (it calls __dev_get_by_index and __bond_opt_set). Postcondition: returns 0 immediately if data is NULL. Otherwise it handles the present attributes in a fixed order (mode, active slave, miimon, updelay, downdelay, peer notif delay, use_carrier, arp interval, arp targets, NS targets, arp validate, arp all targets, primary, primary reselect, fail over mac, xmit hash, resend igmp, peer notif, all slaves active, min links, lp interval, packets per slave, lacp active, lacp rate, ad select, actor sys prio, port key, actor system, tlb dynamic lb, missed max, coupled control, broadcast neigh, lacp strict) and for each calls __bond_opt_set except use_carrier, which is only validated and not applied. It stops at the first failure and returns it, so attributes processed before the failure stay applied. Failures: -ENODEV if IFLA_BOND_ACTIVE_SLAVE is a non-zero ifindex with no such device (an unknown IFLA_BOND_PRIMARY ifindex is not an error: it selects the empty name); -EINVAL if IFLA_BOND_USE_CARRIER is not 1; -EINVAL if a non-zero ARP interval or ARP validate is given in the same message as a non-zero IFLA_BOND_MIIMON (the check uses only the miimon in this message, not the bond's current setting); -EINVAL if an ARP target attribute is shorter than 4 bytes, an IPv6 target attribute shorter than 16 bytes or IFLA_BOND_AD_ACTOR_SYSTEM is not ETH_ALEN bytes long; or the errno returned by __bond_opt_set. For IFLA_BOND_ARP_IP_TARGET the existing target list is cleared first and then re-populated one target at a time (the NS IPv6 list likewise under CONFIG_IPV6), so an error during the loop leaves the list cleared or partly filled, and a warning is logged if no target is set while arp_interval is non-zero. It takes no locks of its own and allocates nothing.
note: Reviewer right: IFLA_BOND_USE_CARRIER is only checked (bond_netlink.c:291-297), no __bond_opt_set call, so 'applies each present attribute through __bond_opt_set' was too broad. Also added: the miimon used in the arp interval/validate check is the local value from this message (255-263, 301, 374); the cleared target lists can stay cleared on error (317-338); unknown primary ifindex is not an error (398-410). Slice 258-511 cut the head and tail; function is 216-614, read in full (lines of the repetitive attribute cases skimmed).

name: AT91_IS(9263)
prose: Generated function at91_is_sam9263 (defined by the AT91_IS(9263) macro invocation, a static inline). Precondition: priv points to a readable struct at91_priv. Postcondition: it returns 1 if priv->devtype_data.type equals AT91_DEVTYPE_SAM9263 and 0 otherwise; it reads only that field, has no side effects and takes no locks.

name: flexcan_exit_stop_mode
prose: Precondition: priv points to an initialised flexcan_priv with valid regs, priv->read and priv->write hooks and devtype_data.quirks; when the SCFW quirk is set priv->scu_idx and priv->sc_ipc_handle are valid, and when only the GPR quirk is set priv->stm.gpr, stm.req_gpr and stm.req_bit are valid. Postcondition: if the SCFW quirk is set it calls flexcan_stop_mode_enable_scfw(priv, false) (which releases the stop request through the SCU firmware); a negative return is returned immediately without touching MCR. If the SCFW call returns 0 or a positive value, or if the SCFW quirk is clear, it continues: when the SCFW quirk is clear and the GPR quirk is set it clears the stop-request bit (1 << req_bit) in the regmap register req_gpr (the regmap_update_bits result is ignored); with only the SCMI quirk, or no quirk, no stop request is touched. It then clears FLEXCAN_MCR_SLF_WAK in the MCR register and returns the result of flexcan_low_power_exit_ack, which polls MCR for up to FLEXCAN_TIMEOUT_US/10 iterations of 10 microseconds and returns 0 once LPM_ACK is clear or -ETIMEDOUT if it is still set. It takes no lock and transfers no reference or memory.

name: mcp251xfd_irq
prose: Precondition: dev_id is the struct mcp251xfd_priv registered as this threaded IRQ's data, with its regmaps, RX rings (at least rx[0]), TX ring, optional rx_int GPIO and RX offload initialised. Postcondition: handled starts as IRQ_NONE. If priv->rx_int is set it reads the GPIO; while it reads as pending it sets regs_status.rxif to the first RX FIFO bit, runs the rxif handler and sets handled to IRQ_HANDLED, and repeats only if there is exactly one RX ring (it stops on a not-pending read). It then loops: it reads the status registers; the pending set is the interrupt flags that are also enabled; if none is pending it calls can_rx_offload_threaded_irq_finish and returns handled (IRQ_HANDLED if any pass or the GPIO loop handled something, otherwise IRQ_NONE). Otherwise it first acknowledges only the pending flags that are in MCP251XFD_REG_INT_IF_CLEARABLE_MASK with a regmap_update_bits write, then calls the handler for each pending flag in the order MODIF, RXIF, TEFIF, RXOVIF, TXATIF, IVMIF, SERRIF, ECCIF, SPICRCIF, then the CERRIF handler if CERRIF is pending or the CAN state is worse than ERROR_ACTIVE; if the state is BUS_OFF after that CERRIF handler it finishes the RX offload and returns IRQ_HANDLED at once. Otherwise it sets handled to IRQ_HANDLED and reads the status again (the loop has no other exit). Any error from the GPIO-loop handler, the status read, the acknowledge write or any handler jumps to out_fail, which finishes the RX offload, logs 'IRQ handler returned <err>' with netdev_err (for every kind of error, register access or handler), dumps the chip state, disables the chip interrupts, stops the timestamp worker, and returns handled as it stood (IRQ_HANDLED if anything had already been handled, otherwise IRQ_NONE).
note: Reviewers: round-0 'only clearable pending interrupts are acked' right (mcp251xfd-core.c:1514-1523) and the old prose already said it; round-2 'register errors go to out_fail without logging' wrong, all goto out_fail paths (1478, 1494, 1522, ...) reach the netdev_err at 1608; round-15 'out_fail does not stop timestamping' wrong, mcp251xfd_timestamp_stop(priv) is at 1612. Added: the rx_int loop errors also go to out_fail, and the loop returns IRQ_HANDLED on BUS_OFF without the interrupt disable (1596-1599). Slice 1270-1524 cut the head; function is 1457-1615, read in full; the mcp251xfd_handle macro and handler bodies were not read.

name: mcp251xfd_handle_tefif
prose: Precondition: priv is the struct mcp251xfd_priv with initialised TEF ring (priv->tef, with its uinc_xfer array of increment transfers), TX ring (priv->tx), SPI device and regmaps, called from the interrupt handler's context (it takes no lock itself). Postcondition: this is mcp251xfd_handle_tefif. It returns 0 on success or a negative errno. It first obtains the number of pending TEF objects len (error from mcp251xfd_get_tef_len returned at once), reads len TEF objects from the chip in one or two SPI reads (the second for the wrapped part; any read error is returned), and handles them one at a time with mcp251xfd_handle_tefif_one, summing the frame lengths. If a handler returns -EBADMSG (the mcp2518fd sequence-number erratum) it stops the loop and the TEFs handled so far (i of them) are treated as good; any other error is returned immediately without advancing ring state. Then, if at least one TEF was handled, it advances ring->head by len (the number handled, as len is overwritten with i), increments the TEF FIFO tail len times with one spi_sync_transfer on the tail of uinc_xfer (an error is returned after ring->head has already been advanced), advances tx_ring->tail by len, calls netdev_completed_queue(len, total_frame_len) and, when CONFIG_CAN_MCP251XFD_SANITY is enabled, compares the chip's TEF tail with its own and returns -EILSEQ (logged) on a mismatch or the error from reading it. It then resets the ECC status (ecc_stat = 0), wakes the netdev queue after a full memory barrier if the TX ring has free space, starts the TX IRQ coalescing hrtimer if tx_coalesce_usecs_irq is non-zero, and returns 0.
note: Not a drop: the packet's name mcp251xfd_handle_tefif_tail is not a function in the source; the slice (tef.c:253-302) is the tail of the real function mcp251xfd_handle_tefif (213-306), so this is a FIX under the real name with the head cut. The old prose was about the tail only and wrong in places: it said ring->head and tx_ring->tail advance by 'len handled TEFs recorded in i' (matches 280-300) but omitted the read/handle loop, the -EBADMSG early exit, the sanity check returning -EILSEQ, the ECC reset and the coalescing timer (213-240, 282-304). I did not read mcp251xfd_handle_tefif_one, get_tef_len or tef_obj_read.

name: ksz_ptp_tou_pulse_verify
prose: Precondition: pulse_ns is a u64 pulse width in nanoseconds smaller than 2^35 (34359738368), so that pulse_ns / 8 fits in the u32 variable data without truncation (larger values would be truncated before the range check and could be accepted wrongly). name: ksz8463_spi_read
prose: Precondition: this is a regmap bus read callback; context is the struct device embedded in a valid spi_device, reg points to at least 2 readable bytes (the code copies a u16 command from reg after the size check, whatever reg_size is), and val points to at least val_size writable bytes; the call may sleep (spi_write_then_read). Postcondition: if reg_size > 2 or val_size > 4 it returns -EINVAL without touching val. Otherwise it builds the command with ksz8463_reg(cmd, val_size), encodes it big-endian in a 2-byte buffer, calls spi_write_then_read sending reg_size command bytes and reading val_size bytes into val, and returns that call's result: 0 on success, or its negative errno, in which case val may be partly or wholly unwritten (its contents are unspecified). On a big-endian build, after a successful read with val_size equal to 2 or 4, the value is converted in place from little-endian to host order; for val_size 1 and 3 (and on little-endian builds) val is left as read. It holds no lock and retains no reference or allocation.
note: Reviewers: round-2 right (ksz_spi.c:73 always copies 2 bytes from reg, so the old reg_size-based wording was wrong); round-15 right (only val_size 2 or 4 are converted, 82-92, val_size 3 is not). The old prose said 'converted ... when val_size > 1', fixed. The earliest reviewer (contract omits SPI errors) is moot, there is no contract; the negative errno from spi_write_then_read is returned at 94. I did not read ksz8463_reg or spi_write_then_read.

name: qca8k_phy_eth_command
prose: Precondition: priv, priv->bus and priv->mgmt_eth_data are valid and initialised (the completion, mutex and sequence counter), phy and regnum identify an MDIO register, and the caller may sleep and holds neither priv->bus->mdio_lock nor mgmt_eth_data->mutex. Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL immediately if regnum >= QCA8K_MDIO_MASTER_MAX_REG (nothing locked or allocated). It then allocates three skbs (write, clear, read); if any allocation fails it frees the ones already allocated and returns -ENOMEM before any lock is taken. It takes priv->bus->mdio_lock (nested) and then mgmt_eth_data->mutex; if priv->mgmt_conduit is NULL it releases both, frees all three skbs and returns -EINVAL without sending anything. Otherwise it sends the MDIO master write command and waits for the completion: on timeout it returns -ETIMEDOUT and on a missing ack -EINVAL (both after freeing read_skb); otherwise it busy-waits for the MDIO master BUSY bit to clear by polling with copies of the read skb; if the poll fails and the busy-wait helper's own return is negative that negative errno is returned (the helper gives -ENOMEM, -ETIMEDOUT or -EINVAL) and read_skb is not freed on that path (a leak); if the poll timed out while the helper itself succeeded, ret stays -ETIMEDOUT for a write (for a read it is overwritten below). For a read it then sends read_skb (the skb is consumed by dev_queue_xmit), waits for the completion and returns -ETIMEDOUT on timeout, -EINVAL if not acked, or mgmt_eth_data->data[0] & QCA8K_MDIO_MASTER_DATA_MASK on success; for a write read_skb is freed and the result is 0 on success. Every path that got past the mgmt_conduit check (success and failure alike) then goes to exit: it sends clear_skb (consumed by dev_queue_xmit) to reset the MDIO master, waits up to the timeout for its completion (the wait's result is ignored), releases mgmt_eth_data->mutex and then priv->bus->mdio_lock, and returns the value computed above. write_skb is consumed by dev_queue_xmit on those paths; no lock is held on return.
note: Reviewers: all three right in part. (1) round 0: the early returns (633-634, 652-653, 657-660, 664-667, 688-693) skip the reset; (2) round 2: the reset runs on every post-lock path including success (764-775); (3) round 15: the exit path transmits clear_skb rather than freeing it, and read_skb may already be consumed (743, 715, 721, 762); the old 'frees all internally allocated sk_buffs' is wrong. Also found: the goto exit at qca8k-8xxx.c:730-733 leaves read_skb unfreed and unsent (leak), because qca8k_phy_eth_busy_wait (586-620) works on skb_copy copies only. Slice 511-766 cut the head and tail; function is 622-791, read in full. I did not read qca8k_alloc_mdio_header; the uninitialised use of val if the helper fails on the first poll pass is not claimed.

name: sja1105_vl_stats
prose: Precondition: priv, rule, stats and extack (which may be NULL as NL_SET_ERR_MSG_MOD tolerates) are valid pointers, priv->info->regs is valid, port identifies a port of the switch, and rule->vl.stats.pkts and rule->vl.stats.lastused hold the previously reported packet count and jiffies timestamp; the call may sleep (SPI transfer). Postcondition: this is sja1105_vl_stats. It returns 0 without reading hardware or touching stats or rule->vl.stats if the rule's VL type is not SJA1105_VL_TIME_TRIGGERED or if sja1105_find_vlid finds no virtual link for this port and key (a negative vlid). Otherwise it reads the SJA1105_SIZE_VL_STATUS-byte VL status from register vl_status + 2 * vlid over SPI; if that transfer fails it sets the extack message 'SPI access failed' and returns the negative errno without modifying rule->vl.stats or stats. On success it unpacks the timing-error, unreleased and length-error counters, sums them as pkts, calls flow_stats_update(stats, 0 bytes, pkts - rule->vl.stats.pkts packets, 0 drops, jiffies - rule->vl.stats.lastused as the last-used delta, FLOW_ACTION_HW_STATS_IMMEDIATE), then stores pkts in rule->vl.stats.pkts and the current jiffies in rule->vl.stats.lastused, and returns 0.
note: Not a drop: the slice sja1105_vl.c:788-802 is the tail of the real function sja1105_vl_stats (762-805), so it is a FIX under the real name with the slice cut at the head. The old prose omitted the two early return-0 cases (type check at 772-773, vlid lookup at 775-777); it said the delta is reported after 'unpacking' counters, which matches 786-795.

name: pop_tx_status
prose: Precondition: dev is a valid network device of the 3c574 card with dev->base_addr the I/O base, the card's TX status register readable at ioaddr + TxStatus, the register window already set as the callers need, and the caller holds lp->window_lock (both callers in this file, tc574_start_xmit at 740-759 and the interrupt handler at 781-850, do). Postcondition: returns void. It loops at most 32 times; each time it reads the TX status byte and stops without popping if bits 0x84 are both clear. Otherwise, if any of bits 0x30 is set it resets the transmitter with tc574_wait_for_completion(dev, TxReset); if any of bits 0x38 is set (this includes every status with a 0x30 bit set) it logs a debug message, issues TxEnable to the command register and increments dev->stats.tx_aborted_errors; then it writes 0 to TxStatus to pop that entry. It acquires and releases no lock, so the caller's lp->window_lock stays held, and it returns no value.
note: Reviewers: round 2 right (the caller holds window_lock, 3c574_cs.c:740/758 and 781/804). Round 0 and round 15: the 0x30 vs 0x38 distinction is real (717 vs 719) but round-15's claim that a 0x30 entry can be reset without being logged is wrong: 0x30 is a subset of 0x38 (0x10 and 0x20 are inside 0x38), so every entry that is reset is also logged, re-enabled and counted. Old prose was right on this and is kept, tightened to say the loop is a 'stops without popping' case. Slice 514-773 cut the head; function is 706-727. I did not read tc574_wait_for_completion.

name: typhoon_request_firmware
prose: Precondition: tp points to a valid struct typhoon whose pdev and dev are valid; the file-scope typhoon_fw is NULL or holds a firmware image cached by an earlier successful call; the caller is in process context (request_firmware sleeps) and serialises calls (typhoon_fw is unlocked global state). Postcondition: if typhoon_fw is already non-NULL it returns 0 at once, without checking or requesting anything. Otherwise it calls request_firmware for FIRMWARE_NAME; on failure it logs an error and returns that negative errno (request_firmware is expected to leave typhoon_fw NULL then; not read here). On success it checks that the image is at least sizeof(struct typhoon_file_header) bytes and that the first 8 bytes of the tag equal 'TYPHOON'; then for each of numSections sections (count from the header) it checks that at least sizeof(struct typhoon_section_header) bytes remain and that the section length is not larger than the remaining count, and moves on past the header and body. The remaining count is reduced by each section body but not by the section-header sizes, so an image whose sections plus headers exceed the file can pass the check (the check is weaker than 'every section fits'). If every check passes it returns 0 with typhoon_fw holding the cached image, which the caller must not release. If any check fails it logs 'Invalid firmware image', calls release_firmware, sets typhoon_fw to NULL and returns -EINVAL.
note: Reviewer right: typhoon.c:1306-1313 advances image_data past the section header but only subtracts section_len from remaining (not the header size), so a truncated image can be accepted; the old prose claiming every header and body fits was too strong. Slice 1278-1529 started after the signature (function is 1267-1323), so the head was cut. The old claim that typhoon_fw is NULL after request_firmware failure is not visible in this function; hedged.

name: ax_interrupt
prose: Precondition: dev_id points to a valid net_device (the AX88190 PCMCIA card) whose base_addr and netdev_priv ei_device are valid, the card stays in register page 0, and the caller does not hold ei_local->page_lock. Postcondition: it takes page_lock with spin_lock_irqsave and releases it before every return. If ei_local->irqlock is already non-zero it logs an info message with the ISR and IMR values (read only), releases the lock and returns IRQ_NONE, leaving irqlock set and the card registers unchanged. Otherwise it writes 0 to EN0_ISR, sets irqlock to 1 and loops while the ISR read is non-zero and ++nr_serviced < MAX_SERVICE (so at most MAX_SERVICE-1 serviced iterations). In an iteration, if the interface is not running or the status is 0xff it warns, writes that status back to EN0_ISR, sets the local status to 0 and leaves the loop without servicing and without setting handled; otherwise it sets handled to 1, acknowledges the status with the AX88190 workaround (up to 10 write/clear retries on EN0_ISR), runs ei_rx_overrun for an overrun or else ei_receive for RX or RX error, ei_tx_intr for TX or else ei_tx_err for TX error, and adds the three counter registers into the stats on ENISR_COUNTERS. After the loop, status is non-zero only if the loop ended because nr_serviced reached MAX_SERVICE; in that case, only when netif_msg_intr is enabled, it sets handled to 1 and, as nr_serviced >= MAX_SERVICE, warns 'Too much work' unless the status is 0xff and writes ENISR_ALL to EN0_ISR (the other branch, an 'unknown interrupt' warning with a 0xff acknowledge, is not reachable from this state); with netif_msg_intr disabled that leftover is neither logged nor acknowledged and handled is unchanged. It then clears irqlock, writes ENISR_ALL to EN0_IMR, unlocks and returns IRQ_RETVAL(handled): IRQ_HANDLED if any iteration was serviced or the leftover block set it, else IRQ_NONE (for example when ISR reads 0 at entry or the first read is the stopped-card/0xff case).
note: Reviewers: round 0 right (irqlock path returns IRQ_NONE with irqlock left set, axnet_cs.c:1106-1120; the stopped-card branch only writes the status back, 1133-1138); round 2 right (leftover handling is under netif_msg_intr, 1171); round 15 right (handled can already be 1 from serviced iterations when the leftover block is skipped). The old return-value summary said leftover with netif_msg_intr false gives IRQ_NONE, which is wrong. Not claiming the 'unknown interrupt' branch is reachable: with nr_serviced < MAX_SERVICE the loop only exits on status 0 or the break, both leaving status 0 (1130-1138, 1171-1186). Slice 1027-1304 cut the head; function is 1088-1195, read in full; I did not read ei_receive, ei_tx_intr or ei_rx_overrun.

name: airoha_dev_xmit
prose: Precondition: this is airoha_dev_xmit, the ndo_start_xmit callback; skb is the packet to send on dev, dev's private data points to a valid airoha_gdm_port with a valid qdma, the caller does not hold the selected queue's q->lock, and the TX queue chosen for the packet should have been initialised with a non-zero descriptor count (if q->ndesc is 0, WARN_ON_ONCE fires and the packet is dropped). Postcondition: it returns NETDEV_TX_BUSY without consuming skb only when, under q->lock, the queue lacks room (q->queued + 1 + nr_frags >= q->ndesc); it then stops the netdev TX queue, sets q->txq_stopped, releases the lock and returns, leaving ownership with the caller. Every other path returns NETDEV_TX_OK and consumes skb. The packet is dropped (dev_kfree_skb_any and dev->stats.tx_dropped incremented) if skb_cow_head fails for a GSO packet (before the lock), if q->ndesc is 0 (before the lock), or if a dma_map_single fails (the entries already mapped in this call are unmapped and returned to the queue's free list under the lock, which is then released). On success each fragment is DMA-mapped into a descriptor taken from q->tx_list, the skb pointer is stored only in the entry of the last fragment (it is freed later by the TX completion path, not here, and not read in this function), q->queued is increased by the fragment count, the queue is stopped if fewer than q->free_thr descriptors remain, and the hardware CPU index register is updated if the queue is stopped or there is no xmit_more hint; the lock is released before returning. q->lock is acquired with spin_lock_bh and released on every path that acquires it.
note: Not a drop: the packet's unnamed function is the real airoha_dev_xmit (airoha_eth.c:2008-2154); slice 2045-2295 starts mid-function, so this is a FIX under the real name with the head cut. Old prose errors: it said skb is freed with dev_kfree_skb_any 'after all its fragments have been queued' on success, but on success skb is stored in the last fragment's queue entry (e->skb = skb) and kept until TX completion; I did not read the completion path. Also the old 'dropped if the queue has no descriptors' is right (WARN_ON_ONCE then goto error), but the drops before the lock also include skb_cow_head failure for GSO packets. name: au1000_mii_probe
prose: Precondition: dev is a net_device whose private data is a valid struct au1000_private with a registered aup->mii_bus, the caller is in process context (phy_connect may sleep), and, when aup->phy_static_config is set, aup->mac_id is 0 or 1 (a BUG_ON fires otherwise). Postcondition: if aup->phy_static_config is set it returns 0 without attaching any PHY: after the BUG_ON on mac_id, a non-zero aup->phy_addr only causes a lookup whose result is discarded, and a zero phy_addr logs 'using PHY-less setup'. Otherwise it scans aup->mii_bus for PHY addresses 0 to PHY_MAX_ADDR-1 and picks the first PHY found, or the highest-addressed one when aup->phy_search_highest_addr is set. If none was found and aup->phy1_search_mac0 is set and aup->mac_id is 1, it logs 'no PHY found on MAC1' and enters a loop that looks up each address on the same aup->mii_bus, but because the loop sits under the mac_id == 1 test its first statement 'if (aup->mac_id == 1) break;' exits on the first iteration (mac_id is 1 inside this block), so the loop selects no PHY. If no PHY was selected it logs 'no PHY found' and returns -1. Otherwise it hits BUG_ON if the selected PHY already has an attached_dev, calls phy_connect with au1000_adjust_link and PHY_INTERFACE_MODE_MII and, if that returns an error pointer, logs 'Could not attach to PHY' and returns PTR_ERR of it; on success it limits the PHY to SPEED_100, sets aup->old_link = 0, aup->old_speed = 0 and aup->old_duplex = -1, logs the attached info with phy_attached_info and returns 0.
note: Reviewers: round 0 (the loop uses aup->mii_bus, not a MAC0 bus) is right (au1000_eth.c:511-512) but moot; round 15 is wrong: the break at 514-515 is inside the guard 'aup->mac_id == 1' from line 501, so it always fires on the first pass and the skip-attached logic at 518-526 is dead code. The old prose said this correctly and is kept with reworded detail. Slice 260-513 cut the head; function is 472-556, read in full.

name: lance_probe1
prose: Precondition: this is lance_probe1(dev, ioaddr, irq, options), an __init function called in process context with an unregistered net_device dev, an I/O port base ioaddr at which the caller has exclusive access, and irq non-zero only for PCI cards; chip_table and lance_need_isa_bounce_buffers are initialised. Postcondition: it returns 0 after detecting a LANCE-compatible chip at ioaddr, reading the station address into dev->dev_addr and setting dev->base_addr, dev->irq, dev->dma (4 meaning no ISA DMA channel needed), dev->netdev_ops, dev->watchdog_timeo and dev->ml_priv (a kzalloc'ed lance_private holding a kmalloc_array'ed rx_buffs and, when lance_need_isa_bounce_buffers is set, tx_bounce_buffs), and registering dev with register_netdev; on success the driver keeps lp, its buffers and any requested DMA channel. Failures: -ENOMEM if the ioremap of the BIOS area fails, if kzalloc of lp fails, or if kmalloc_array of rx_buffs or tx_bounce_buffs fails (err is initialised to -ENOMEM and is not changed before those allocations); -ENODEV if CSR0 does not read 0x0004 after reset, if the chip-version signature check fails, if IRQ probing finds no IRQ, if request_dma fails for a preset channel, if automatic DMA detection finds no channel, or if the 7990 IRQ probe fails; or the error returned by register_netdev. Failures before the lp allocation leave dev->base_addr and the station address already modified but allocate nothing. Failures after the lp allocation free tx_bounce_buffs (kfree of NULL is a no-op), rx_buffs and lp and, for the last failure causes (register_netdev failure and the 7990 IRQ probe), also free the DMA channel when dev->dma is not 4; dev stays unregistered; dev->ml_priv is left pointing at the freed lp, so the caller must not use it, and dev->base_addr, dev->dev_addr, dev->irq and dev->dma may have been changed.
note: Reviewer wrong: the round-15 claim that the rx_buffs/tx_bounce_buffs failures return err 'not -ENOMEM' is wrong, because err is initialised to -ENOMEM (lance.c:482) and only set to -ENODEV later at about line 625, after the allocation gotos at 548 and 553; so those paths return -ENOMEM (out_lp/out_rx return err). Also checked: the DMA channel is freed only in out_dma (register_netdev or 7990-IRQ failure), not on the earlier request_dma failure (it did not get the channel) nor on out_tx from the IRQ-probe failure. Slice 508-760 cut the head (function is 472-752), so the real name is lance_probe1 and I read the whole function except comments; I did not read lance_open or the helpers.
